claims.statement: openapi/powercontext.yaml is the source of truth for the HTTP API contract; the Python files under src/powercontext/http/_generated (models.py, operations.py, schema.py) are generated from it by scripts/generate_api.py and must not be hand-edited, but regenerated with make api-generate.

Generated API drift is a gate: scripts/generate_api.py --check fails with a regenerate instruction, make version-check runs api-generate-check and js-api-generate-check, and make check depends on version-check, so stale generated code fails the main quality gate.

The TypeScript operation tables are generated from the OpenAPI contract by scripts/generate_js_operations.py into operations.generated.ts for the DSH, OpenCode, and Pi integrations, and into mcp-operations.generated.ts for DSH; the js-test and opencode-test targets fail through git diff when committed generated output is stale.

integrations/capabilities.toml is the declared integration contract: scripts/integration_manifest.py requires every integrations/ directory to be declared or explicitly excluded (the current exclusions are cindy, agent-plugin, opendal, and lifecycle), checks the per-locale integration documentation pointers, and validates declared tool surfaces, while scripts/generate_integration_manifest_docs.py writes the en and zh capabilities.md pages from it.

The per-host powercontext-project-context skill copies are derived: scripts/integration_guidance_skills.py copies the shared agent-plugin skill into each native host package and retains only each host's references/host.md, and make integration-guidance-check verifies those copies without modifying files.
The Dify plugin contract declaration (powercontext_dify/contract.json) is produced by integrations/dify/generate_contract.py, and make dify-test verifies it with the generator's --check mode.

The Server composes its ASGI application in create_server_app, which mounts every route using the generated operation objects and serves the runtime OpenAPI document from the generated OPENAPI_SCHEMA, so the served contract is the generated one.

The top-level powercontext package re-exports the stable client types, and its PowerContext facade binds Sources, Artifacts, and triggers as three explicitly selected component groups without owning their lifecycle.

Installed commands are declared in pyproject.toml: powercontext maps to powercontext.cli.app:main, powercontext-ops maps to powercontext.ops.__main__:main, and the powercontext.cli entry-point group registers the code, config, doctor, observability, service, server, setup, and archive subcommands.

The built-in runtime is the domain composition root: open_builtin_runtime in builtin/runtime/composition.py is shared by the Server factory and the server CLI, and the project rules require domain behavior to stay in the owning runtime or Artifact service while transport and host adapters only translate.

Network transport safety is centralized in src/powercontext/transport.py: plaintext HTTP is accepted by default only for loopback hosts, and the same policy is intended for the Client SDK, the CLI, and agent integrations, while an unauthenticated Server must not bind to a routable address without its separate opt-in.

The Docker image is a two-stage uv build that installs the cli, server, and tracing-otlp extras from the frozen lock file, requires the POWERCONTEXT_VERSION build argument, runs as a non-root powercontext user with /data as POWERCONTEXT_HOME, exposes port 8000, defaults to 'powercontext server run', and health-checks /health/ready.

The Helm chart deploys the same application image as two Deployments, api and background, each running 'server run' against an external OceanBase database with a Recreate rollout; it does not support SQLite or embedded seekdb, and database initialization via server db-migrate must happen before the first install.

The reference observability stack in deploy/observability is a demonstration with generated local secrets and a real Server started by run-host.py, and its verify.py checks stored traces, logs, and metrics; a receiver port or healthy container alone is not accepted as evidence.

The personal service bootstrap in src/powercontext_service_bootstrap/__main__.py applies a persisted bounded retry budget to each launch attempt before importing the PowerContext service launcher, and the launchd adapter invokes this bootstrap module with the retry arguments.
The ops entry point powercontext-ops runs one bounded JSON request per independent process, requiring either a private operator target-binding file or a private producer catalog file.

The gateway under gateway/ is an optional Rust workspace of seven crates; pc-gateway-core holds the two-phase gate executor state machine, pc-gateway-app is the thin binary, and the gateway does not own policy because every allow, block, or refuse decision comes from PowerContext Core.

The gateway supports two deployment forms selected by environment: combined mode uses PC_GATEWAY_CORE_UDS and reverse-proxies non-/gateway traffic to Core over a Unix socket, while standalone mode uses PC_GATEWAY_CORE_BASE to reach a remote Core directly.

Host integrations under integrations/ are thin clients for a running PowerContext Server and do not embed storage; the Codex plugin, for example, reaches the Server through hooks and Streamable HTTP MCP.

Release references are synchronized by scripts/release_version.py (including the OpenAPI info.version), and make version-bump then regenerates the API code, while distribution versions still come from Git tags.

Focused contract tests guard the generated and declared surfaces: tests/test_api_contract.py, tests/test_js_operations.py, and tests/test_desktop_contract.py run under make contract-test after the drift checks, and tests/test_integration_manifest.py runs under make integration-manifest-check.

The Server's authorization policy lives in the built-in package builtin/authz (access service, repositories, profiles, and Casbin/AuthZen backends); server/ mounts and enforces that service, while server/authentication.py resolves bearer identities.

The desktop application is a Tauri 2 shell whose Rust side registers a fixed set of native commands, owns connection profiles (profiles.json in the app data directory) and Bearer credentials stored in the OS vault through keyring, and fails closed when another process owns the profile storage.
The desktop React UI reaches the native shell only through the wrappers in desktop/ui/src/shared (Tauri invoke and the ops-progress event) and uses types from the generated ui/src/generated/ipc.ts.

desktop/scripts/generate.mjs generates the desktop contract from openapi/powercontext.yaml into ui/src/generated/api.d.ts, ui/src/generated/operations.ts, src-tauri/src/transport/wire.rs, and src-tauri/src/transport/operations.json; with --check it fails on drift and asks for pnpm --dir desktop generate.
The desktop IPC type file ui/src/generated/ipc.ts is written by the export_ipc example from Rust ts-rs declarations, and its --check mode (pnpm --dir desktop ipc:check) fails on drift.

scripts/prepare_desktop_product.py reads the producer's immutable Ops bundle and single Server resource catalog, verifies their digests and version/platform binding, and publishes a staging directory only after verification succeeds.

The DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin is a client of a running Server: model-facing operations are exposed only through DSH's native MCP as mcp__powercontext__<operation>, automatic recall calls POST /v1/context/prepare once per turn, and the plugin registers no direct HTTP operation tools.

The Dify integration is an isolated SDK plugin under integrations/dify/plugin that exposes pc_* tools, is declared experimental in the manifest, and its contract is generated and checked by make dify-test together with ruff, ty, and pytest.

The WorkBuddy integration is a thin client: a UserPromptSubmit hook driver implemented in pure Python standard library prepares bounded context and captures the prompt, MCP is served over Streamable HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp, and the installer powercontext setup workbuddy writes the hook, MCP entry, and Skill.

The Kimi Code integration is an experimental native plugin with minimal, recommended, and full tool profiles; it resolves Scope on the Server from explicit configuration, then workspace binding, then the Server default, and its prompt hook does not flush Memory.

The Cindy integration is excluded from the integration manifest; its hook worker is built with tsdown from the DSH toolchain, the committed worker.cjs is verified by git diff in make cindy-test, and the packaged .cindy archive is produced by integrations/cindy/scripts/package.py. Native MCP calls through Cindy cannot have Scope arguments enforced by the Ghost.

The ZCode integration is declared in the manifest with prompt, SessionStart, and Stop hooks; prompt and SessionStart hooks allow 3 seconds per HTTP request within a shared 4-second budget and a 5-second host timeout, while Stop processing of pending Sources is disabled by default and uses a 1000 ms budget when enabled.

The OpenDAL integration (powercontext-connector-opendal) is an excluded, independently deployed evaluation Connector worker: it registers an immutable Definition manifest, advances the binding checkpoint only after every accepted snapshot has a durable Server receipt and the scan has no rejected or failed items, and is not a complete standard Source integration.

The Pydantic AI integration is an experimental preview adapter built on the public asynchronous Python Client; it provides three tools, prepares context before model requests, and is type-checked by make workflow-actions-check.

Shared lifecycle helpers have a single source: integrations/lifecycle/transport.ts and src/powercontext_integration_lifecycle are copied by scripts/generate_integration_lifecycle.py into the host plugins that ship them, and make integration-lifecycle-check runs inside make check to reject drifted copies.

The examples/ directory holds runnable reference code outside the wheel packages declared in pyproject.toml; each example has its own entry point, such as the Jupyter tutorials (make notebooks, make notebooks-test), the OpenAI SDK chat.py, and the systemone DecisionModel adapter injected into open_builtin_runtime.
